HC-MoE v8: What the Held-Out and Compute-Ratio Experiments Found

Experiments 1 and 3 from v7 — and the correction to the Q75 slice they exposed
October 4, 2026 · v8
Abstract. This drop carried two experiments proposed in v7: a pre-registered held-out re-run of the Q75 slice (experiment 1) and a within-family sweep of the compute ratio (experiment 3). Reading their scripts showed that “Q75” is not the upper quartile of layers, as this series has said since v5. It is the set of tokens whose Intelligence Gain is above its 75th percentile, and the other “layer subsets” are the same selection at other cut-offs. Selecting on the outcome cannot show that HC predicts it: on identical tokens it raised the HC–IG correlation in 27 of 27 cases and turned a null full-sample correlation (tinystories, +0.001) into +0.121. v7's headline, that Q75 is where the evidence is strongest, is withdrawn. Two further errors pushed the same way: the full-network cells were graded at n = 10,000, which is the size of the Monte-Carlo simulation rather than the sample (median n = 51,100), and v6 used a different HC statistic from the rest of the series. Graded at its measured effective sample size, the full network carries 13 tier-A Intelligence Gain cells, not 5. On that clean slice the series' core results hold and firm up: HC tracks token difficulty in all four families; Qwen's positive association with IG (best cell Qwen/lambada, r = +0.129, 95% CI +0.118–+0.140) keeps 88% of its magnitude when the single strongest expert is partialled out. Experiment 3 settles one question cleanly: holding Qwen's large model fixed and shrinking the compute gap to Gemma's level (1.9×) leaves the association positive in all nine benchmarks, so Gemma's inversion is not a small-gap effect; the gap scales the size of the association, and it does so entirely through the small model. Experiment 1's IG-selected correlations reproduce on held-out passages (r = +0.97 across 36 cells), which shows they are stable, not that they are meaningful as prediction.

1. Research goals and where the study stands

The two primary questions

  1. Does HC track token difficulty? r(HC, CEbig) and r(HC, CEsmall), answered first.
  2. Does HC track Intelligence Gain? r(HC, IG), IG = CEsmall − CEbig.

Null estimator, HC variant, control and statistic are secondary axes: checks on those two answers, not findings of their own. The fifth axis this series has used, the “layer subset”, turns out not to exist in the data, which is the main subject of this report.

What this drop changes

Three statements this series has made since v5 are wrong, and all three are now corrected

1. The Q50–Q95 slices select tokens on Intelligence Gain, not on layer depth. Both experiment scripts define the slice explicitly — mask = IG >= percentile(IG, 75) — and keep 25.0% of tokens in every one of 99 rows. Experiment 3's Q75 values reproduce the original 26_08_30 Q75 column to four decimals (8 of 9 benchmarks, correlation 0.9998), so the original columns are the same selection. Every report from v5 onward, including the profile this series is built from, called these “upper-layer quantile subsets”; I carried that label into v6 and v7 without checking it against the pipeline.

2. The 26_08_30 drop is the full corpus, not a 10,000-token subsample. Its full-network correlations are identical to the 26_09_03 max_20pct correlations in 1296 of 1296 rows. The “10,000” in its null file name is the simulation length. v5 through v7 graded every cell at that n, which made the full network look weaker than it is and the IG-selected slices look stronger.

3. The series' HC statistic, Max_Per_Row, is max_20pct — the maximum over the top 20% of experts. v6 headlined the max statistic instead, so its estimator findings (GMM as Qwen's outlier) came from a different statistic. With the right one, GLM is the outlier in every family where the spread matters.

What this does not affect. The data are sound: the grid is complete, the sign convention passes its arithmetic check in every testable row of all three drops, and the two experiments ran as designed. What changes is what the Q-slices mean, and the sample size every earlier grade assumed. The fix is to move the primary analysis back to the full token set, where both drops agree exactly and the effective sample size is measured. Everything in sections 5–11 is computed there.

Main findings so far

What the project holds after eight reports. Each claim carries its tier and the version it was established in; where this cycle withdrew part of a claim, the evidence line says so. Every Intelligence Gain claim carries one qualification that has not moved since v4: corr(gap, IG) = 0.96, so at summary level the IG signal is very nearly the difficulty gap.

Recorded as each check ran. Three are new this cycle: the definition audit that found the problem, the sign invariant applied to both experiments, and the out-of-sample replication. The block-bootstrap null moves from partial to done because the primary slice is back on the full token set, where it was measured.

Statistic definition auditv8Whether each slice and statistic is what the report says it isdoneThree corrections. (1) ‘Q75’ keeps 25.0% of tokens, chosen by IG ≥ its 75th percentile — selection on the outcome, not upper layers. (2) Max_Per_Row is max_20pct (identical in 432/432 cells). (3) The 26_08_30 drop is the full corpus, not a 10,000-token subsample.

Replicates — but what replicates is an IG-selected quantity. The split is sequential, not random.
Still not run: rank and heavy-tail robustness. It has been open since v1 and is now the most pressing gap. The IG-selected slices nearly double r where normal theory says they should halve it, and the empirical decile lift in experiment 3 is 1.5× the normal-theory formula. Both are what a few heavy-tailed tokens carrying the Pearson correlation would produce. It is the first experiment in section 14.

Grading at the real sample size reverses the series' picture of the full network

v5 through v7 graded every correlation at n = 10,000, read from the Monte-Carlo null's file name. The real nominal n runs from 12,314 to 477,782 tokens (median 51,100), and the measured effective n after autocorrelation has a median of 23,506 on the IG target. Median deflation is 2.61× across all targets (IQR 1.83–3.22, max 5.98×): 2.82 for CEbig, 2.69 for CEsmall, 2.29 for IG. Thresholds widen by √deflation, about 1.6×. It is structured by text: mmlu 3.52× and competition_math 3.47× at the top, hellaswag 1.07× at the bottom.

Fisher-z of the 432 full-network IG configurations at each cell's measured ESS. σ0 = 4.93; the same correlations give 7.44 at true nominal n and 11.97 at the old n = 10,000. What remains is real between-family heterogeneity — the families differ in sign.

Selecting tokens on Intelligence Gain inflates their correlation with HC

Experiment 3 computed both slices on the same tokens, which makes the effect of the selection directly visible. The IG-selected correlation exceeds the full-sample one in 27 of 27 benchmark × model cases, by a median factor of 1.9 where both are clearly non-zero. For a bivariate-normal pair, keeping the top quartile of one variable would shrink the correlation to roughly half; here it nearly doubles.

The starkest case is tinystories with the 0.6B partner: +0.0010 on all tokens, +0.1206 among the top quartile of IG. A correlation of that size would have been graded tier A in v7. hellaswag with the 4B partner goes from -0.0003 to +0.0922.

Across the original 26_08_30 grid the selection shows the same signature as the cut tightens: the signed mean over all 432 configurations climbs from +0.0024 (all tokens) to +0.0465 (top 10%), and the number of positive cells from 19 to 27 of 36. v7 read that drift as “Q75 shifts the grid toward positive” and attributed it to upper layers. It is the selection.

Experiment 1: the IG-selected correlations reproduce

Experiment 1 pre-registered the slice (Q75, GMM, standard, max_20pct) and split each benchmark's passages into an exploratory first half and a held-out second half. Under that identical protocol the two halves agree closely: across the 36 cells the IG correlations correlate +0.970, 92% agree in sign, mean |r| moves from 0.0781 to 0.0759, tier A from 8 to 7, and 26 of 36 held-out cells have a bootstrap CI excluding zero against 26 exploratory.

Figure 6 — Experiment 1: exploratory against held-out, 36 cells

Points on the dashed diagonal reproduce exactly. They sit close to it in every family.

How to read the ‘attenuated’ verdict. The script compared its held-out tier-A count (7) with v7's 13 and returned “attenuated, inconclusive”. That benchmark was graded at the wrong n on twelve-configuration means; experiment 1 grades one configuration on half the passages. Like for like, exploratory against held-out, there is no attenuation. And reproducing is not the same as being meaningful: a selection on the outcome reproduces as reliably as any other computation. The split is also sequential rather than random, so the halves may share whatever ordering the corpora have.

What the IG-selected numbers can still say: among tokens where the large model already wins by a wide margin, HC tracks how wide that margin is. That is a description of the upper tail of IG. It cannot be used to find those tokens, because finding them required knowing IG. The legitimate version of the same question selects on HC instead — does the HC–IG relationship concentrate among strongly anomalous tokens? — and is proposed in section 14.

Q1 — HC tracks token difficulty in every family, with a family-specific sign

Against CEbig: mean |r| 0.0564, 30 of 36 cells outside the measured floor, 13 tier A. Against CEsmall: 0.0670, 27 of 36, 13 tier A.

Qwen, ERNIE and Liquid are positive on both targets; Gemma is negative on both (-0.0342 p<0.01 and -0.0550 p<0.01), so in Gemma anomalous routing marks tokens that are easier for both models. Its IG inversion is already present in the difficulty relationship. Qwen shows the asymmetry that generates an IG correlation: +0.0099 against the large model's loss, +0.0489 p<0.01 against the small model's.

Figure 7 — What HC tracks, by family

Family means over 108 configurations. Dashed lines: measured floor ±0.0128.

Q2 — HC tracks Intelligence Gain; the full network carries 13 tier-A cells

Mean |r| against IG is 0.0466, smaller than either CE target, but better determined: 25 of 36 cells have all twelve configurations agreeing on sign, and tiers come out 13 A, 9 B, 14 C at measured ESS.

By family: Qwen +0.0538 p<0.01, Gemma -0.0500 p<0.01, ERNIE +0.0014, Liquid +0.0045. ERNIE and Liquid average near zero but each has tier-A cells (2 and 3) of opposite signs — cancellation across benchmarks, not absence. The grand mean (+0.0024) is cancellation between families and should not be quoted.

The strongest cell is Qwen/lambada: r = +0.1289 (95% passage-bootstrap CI +0.1180–+0.1395), ESS 33,123, tolerating another 143× deflation, and +0.23 sd of IG in the top HC decile by the normal-theory formula. Experiment 3 measured that lift directly for Qwen and found it a median 1.5× the formula, so the formula understates it.

CIs are means of the twelve configurations' passage-bootstrap intervals.

IG is not yet separated from the difficulty gap. corr(rsmall − rbig, rIG) = 0.963. The defensible phrasing is “HC predicts where the small model struggles more than the large one”. Experiment 3 adds that the association moves entirely with the small model (section 6), which fits that phrasing and does not yet go beyond it.

Secondary axis: controls and statistic

The signal is mostly sparse and clearly multi-expert

Both controls exist at the full network, so for the first time they can be read against a measured floor. Qwen keeps 72% of its IG correlation when the dense Fisher combination is partialled out and 88% when the single strongest expert is; Gemma keeps 48% and 76%. Over the 25 cells more than twice the floor, median retention is 59% under Fisher (sign kept in 88%) and 79% under pmin (sign kept in 100%).

The single strongest expert carries almost nothing on its own: InvMinP stays within ±0.011 in every family. Recomputing HC without that expert keeps a median 59%. So the routing signal is spread across several experts, and a little over half of it is distinct from a broad elevation of every p-value.

Figure 9 — What survives each control, by family

The two conditionings answer different questions and are never averaged. ERNIE and Liquid have no raw family-level effect to retain, so their bars are not read as retention.

Secondary axes: null estimator and HC variant

Material estimator effect: GLM sits +0.0165 from the others and the spread across estimators is 0.0252 in r (permutation p = 0.000) -- at or beyond the 0.0128 noise floor, so a reader could reach a different conclusion depending on the estimator chosen. Show the per-estimator breakdown, say which estimator each headline number came from, and treat the divergence as a result in its own right: it says something about the null-estimation step, not only about the routing signal.

Direction, which the verdict omits: GLM sits -0.0165 below the other five, and it is the deviant in Qwen, ERNIE and Gemma. Dropping it brings the overall spread from 0.0252 to 0.0134, essentially the 0.0128 floor; Qwen falls to 0.0192, ERNIE to 0.0179, while Gemma keeps 0.0296. Liquid (0.0149) is clean with or without it. v7 said the deviant was GMM in Qwen and concluded it was not one bad fit; that came from v6's max statistic. With the series' own statistic, one fit accounts for most of the problem.

Figure 10 — Mean IG correlation under each null estimator (mandatory figure)

Pooled over families, so each bar sits inside the floor through cancellation; the finding is the 0.0252 span, most of it GLM.

Figure 11 — Estimator effect within each family

GLM, at the right, pulls Qwen, ERNIE and Gemma down together. Liquid is flat.

Consistent across variants: highest-to-lowest spread is only 0.0038 in r, well inside the 0.0128 noise floor. The conclusions do not depend on variant choice.

6. Experiment 3: the compute ratio within Qwen

+0.0517
Qwen at Gemma's ~2× gap
9/9
benchmarks still positive
8/9
strictly ordered by ratio
+0.40
cross-family ρ(gap, r), all tokens

v7 asked whether the compute gap between a family's large and small model decides whether HC tracks IG, since the two families near a 2× gap (Liquid, Gemma) were the two without a positive association. Experiment 3 holds Qwen3-30B-A3B fixed — so its routing, and its HC, are unchanged — and swaps the dense small partner between Qwen3-0.6B (5.5×), Qwen3-1.7B (1.9×, Gemma's range) and Qwen3-4B (0.8×, the small model has more active parameters than the large one). The full token set is the clean comparison; the IG-selected slice is shown second because its tokens change with each partner.

The gap scales the association but does not flip it — so it does not explain Gemma

On the full token set Qwen's IG correlation falls with the gap: +0.0641 at 5.5×, +0.0517 at 1.9×, +0.0280 at 0.8×. The ordering is strict in 8 of 9 benchmarks; moving to the 1.7B partner lowers r in 8 of 9 and moving to 4B lowers it in 9 of 9. But at Gemma's gap the association stays positive in all nine benchmarks (7 with a bootstrap CI excluding zero), and even with a larger small model it is positive in 7 of 9.

That answers v7's decision rule directly: the gap is not what separates Gemma from Qwen. A small gap weakens the association; it does not invert it. What remains for Gemma is architectural — its always-active shared expert, and E2B's 2.8B parameters of per-layer embeddings, which give the small model token-specific lookup capacity that a compute ratio does not count.

The mechanism is visible in the decomposition. Because the large model and its HC are fixed, r(HC, CEbig) is identical across partners (+0.0338). All of the change is in r(HC, CEsmall): +0.0790 → +0.0614 → +0.0456. A larger small model struggles less on exactly the tokens the large model's routing flags as anomalous.

Figure 12 — Qwen's association as the small partner grows

Means over nine benchmarks. Ordered by ratio, so lines. The flat CE_big line is the large model held fixed; the falling CE_small line carries the whole IG change. The IG-selected line sits above the rest for the reason given in section 4.

Figure 13 — Per benchmark, all tokens

Eight of nine fall monotonically (tinystories ticks up at 1.9× from a null start). At 0.8× three reach the floor: mmlu and hellaswag inside it, tinystories below it at -0.024 — the only sign change, and only once the small model is the larger of the two.

Three limits. This is one family, one estimator (GMM) and one variant (standard), so it says nothing about whether the same scaling holds in ERNIE or Liquid, and it inherits the GLM question only by not using GLM. The script's own regression treats 27 points as independent; they are nine benchmarks measured three times each, which is why the paired within-benchmark comparison is used here. And across the four families the gap barely orders the associations on the full token set (Spearman +0.40, p = 0.49) — the edited v7's stronger cross-family pattern (+0.80) came from the IG-selected means, where ERNIE looks positive.

CheckStatusResult
Grid completeness & numeric sanitydone432/432 cells, 0 duplicates, 0 unparsed columns. Avg_Inverse_Min_P still overflows (8.1e298) — descriptive only. New: the 26_08_30 full-network correlations and the 26_09_03 max_20pct correlations are identical in 1296/1296 rows (max difference 1e-16), so the two drops are joined exactly.
Monte-Carlo null reproductiondoneσ = 0.009866, crit_05 = 0.01934 reproduces — but it was computed at n = 10,000, which is the simulation size, not the sample size. Real n runs 12,314–477,782 (median 51,100). The iid floor is retired in favour of the measured one.
Empirical (Efron) nulldoneσ0 = 4.9 at measured ESS, 7.4 at true nominal n, 12.0 at the old n = 10,000 assumption. The residual is between-family heterogeneity, not a broken yardstick.
Block-bootstrap nulldoneDone for the primary slice. Passage-level bootstrap (1,000 resamples) on the full token set with the series' own statistic: 358/432 IG configurations exclude 0. Median deflation 2.61×. v7's ‘partial’ status came from bridging onto the Q75 slice, which is retired. (E1/E3 also report a ‘native ESS’ on Q75, but it is computed on non-contiguous kept tokens and is biased upward — 20/72 rows come back at deflation exactly 1.0.)
Multiplicity / effective test countdone1.16 of 12 configurations per cell (mean pairwise r = 0.92); 432 configurations ≈ 42 independent tests.
BH false discovery ratedone350 of 432 full-network IG configurations at q < 0.05 on ESS-honest z. Permutation p-values are not used: 322/432 sit at the 1e-4 floor.
Autocorrelation robustness (ARF)doneGraded at each cell's own measured ESS. 13 of 36 full-network IG cells clear ARF ≥ 20 beyond their measured ESS.
Estimator consistencydoneFail. Spread 0.0252 against the measured 0.0128 floor; GLM -0.0165 from the rest. Per family: Qwen 0.0320 (GLM), ERNIE 0.0266 (GLM), Gemma 0.0419 (GLM), Liquid 0.0149 (StudentT).
HC variant consistencydonePass: spread 0.0038, inside the 0.0128 floor.
Control retention (Fisher, p_min)doneDone in full for the first time with measured ESS. Both controls exist at the full network. Qwen retains 72% under Fisher and 88% under pmin; Gemma 48% and 76%. Across the 25 cells more than twice the floor, median retention is 59% (Fisher) and 79% (pmin). ERNIE and Liquid have no raw effect to retain.
Layer-subset selectiondoneSuperseded by a definition error. The ‘Q50–Q95 layer subsets’ are tokens whose Intelligence Gain is above its 50th–95th percentile (verified in the pipeline code and by an exact reproduction). Selecting on the outcome cannot support a claim that HC predicts it, so the selection question is moot: the primary slice is reset to the full token set.
Effect size (decile lift)doneFormula lift reported for every headline cell. New: E3 measured the lift empirically on the full token set; across 21 Qwen cells with |r| > 0.02 the empirical lift is 1.50× the 1.755·r formula (range -0.65–2.54).
Difficulty-gap confoundpartialcorr(rsmall − rbig, rIG) = 0.963 at the full network. New partial evidence from E3: holding the large model fixed, r(HC, CEbig) is identical across all three small models while r(HC, CEsmall) falls as the small model grows — the IG association moves entirely through the small model. The token-level control has still not run.
Rank / heavy-tail robustnessnot runNeeds the token-level series. More urgent than before: the IG-selected slices nearly double r where bivariate-normal theory says they should halve it, which is what heavy-tail leverage would produce.
Sign-convention invariantdonePass everywhere: E1 0/11, E3 0/8, 26_09_03 max_20pct 0/43 testable rows inconsistent.
Statistic definition auditdoneThree corrections. (1) ‘Q75’ keeps 25.0% of tokens, chosen by IG ≥ its 75th percentile — selection on the outcome, not upper layers. (2) Max_Per_Row is max_20pct (identical in 432/432 cells). (3) The 26_08_30 drop is the full corpus, not a 10,000-token subsample.
Out-of-sample replicationdoneE1, pre-registered (GMM, standard, max_20pct, Q75): exploratory and held-out halves correlate +0.970 across 36 cells, 92% sign agreement, tier A 8→7. Replicates — but what replicates is an IG-selected quantity. The split is sequential, not random.

The same register as section 1, here for reference beside the assessment.

13. Assessment

Holds up

  • HC tracks token difficulty in all four families, 30 and 27 of 36 cells outside a measured floor.
  • Qwen's positive IG association: 9 of 9 benchmarks, best cell +0.129 (CI +0.118–+0.140), and it survives a small compute gap.
  • The signal is multi-expert: 79% median retention under pmin, sign kept in every strong cell, InvMinP near zero.
  • Gemma's inversion is not a compute-gap effect: Qwen at the same gap stays positive in 9 of 9.
  • The full network is the right primary slice: 13 tier-A IG cells at measured ESS, and the two drops agree on it exactly.
  • Data integrity: complete grid; sign convention passes in every testable row of all three drops.

Not yet established

  • The null estimator: spread 0.0252 against a 0.0128 floor, mostly GLM; Gemma keeps 0.0296 without it.
  • “Where scale helps”: corr(gap, IG) = 0.96; still phrased as the difficulty gap.
  • Any claim built on the Q50–Q95 slices, including all of v7's subset comparisons.
  • Effect sizes: the formula understates the lift by about 1.5× for Qwen, which suggests a heavy tail is doing work.
  • Experiment 3's generality: one family, one estimator, one variant.

Open

  • Are these Pearson correlations carried by a few tokens? Open since v1, now the most urgent check.
  • What inverts Gemma? Shared expert or per-layer embeddings; experiment 3 removed the gap.
  • Does HC's relationship with IG concentrate in HC's own upper tail? The valid version of what the Q-slices were trying to ask.
  • Does the full-network grid reproduce on held-out passages? Experiment 1 replicated the IG-selected slice; the clean slice has not been split.
  • Does the gap scale the association in other families? Only Qwen has been swept.

Proposed

Rank and heavy-tail robustness on the full token set

P0 · a few hours, existing parquet
Question
Are the Pearson correlations describing the corpus or a handful of tokens? Open since v1, and two results this cycle point at heavy tails: IG selection nearly doubles r where normal theory halves it, and the empirical decile lift is 1.5× the formula.
Design
For every tier-A full-network IG cell, compute Spearman and 1%-winsorised Pearson beside the raw Pearson on the token series, with the same passage bootstrap.
Statistic
Spearman / Pearson ratio per cell; tier at measured ESS under each.
Decision rule
If Spearman falls below half the Pearson value in any tier-A cell, that cell drops to B and the effect sizes in section 5 are restated on ranks. If the ratio stays above 0.8 throughout, the tier-A list stands as written.

Drop GLM and re-grade

P0 · under an hour, no new data
Question
GLM accounts for most of the estimator spread (0.0252 → 0.0134 without it). Is the series better served by five estimators?
Design
Re-run the battery on the five remaining estimators; separately inspect GLM's fitted null on one Gemma cell to see why it diverges.
Statistic
Tier counts and family means with and without GLM; Gemma's residual spread.
Decision rule
If tier-A cells and family signs are unchanged without GLM, drop it from the default design and report it as a sensitivity. If Gemma's residual 0.0296 persists, Gemma needs an estimator-choice sensitivity attached to every number.

Split the full-network grid into held-out halves

P1 · ~half a day, experiment 1's script with the mask removed
Question
Do the 13 full-network tier-A cells reproduce on passages they were not measured on?
Design
Run experiment 1's protocol with no IG mask, and with a random passage split rather than first half / second half.
Statistic
Exploratory-vs-held-out correlation across cells; tier-A on each half at measured ESS.
Decision rule
If held-out tier-A is within about 3 of exploratory and cell correlations exceed 0.8, the full-network results are confirmed out of sample. If tier-A falls by half, the grid is overfitting passage selection.

Select on HC instead of IG

P1 · an hour, existing data
Question
Does HC's relationship with IG concentrate among strongly anomalous tokens? This is the question the Q-slices were reaching for, asked so that the answer could be used without knowing IG.
Design
Keep tokens with HC at or above its 75th percentile; correlate HC with IG there, on the same tokens as the full-network grid.
Statistic
r(HC, IG | HC ≥ Q75) against the full-network r per cell, against the halving that range restriction alone would produce.
Decision rule
If the HC-selected correlation exceeds the full-network one, the relationship lives in HC's anomalous tail and thresholding HC is the practical design. If it falls by roughly half, the relationship is linear across the range.

Isolate Gemma's inversion

P1 · ~1 day, small-model forward passes
Question
With the compute gap ruled out, is the cause the always-active shared expert or the E2B partner's per-layer embeddings?
Design
Swap Gemma's small partner for a dense model of similar effective size without per-layer embeddings, keeping the large model fixed as in experiment 3.
Statistic
Sign and size of r(HC, IG) and r(HC, CEsmall) with each partner.
Decision rule
If the inversion disappears with a plain dense partner, the per-layer embeddings are the cause and Gemma's result says nothing about its routing. If it persists, the shared expert is the remaining candidate.

Token-level control for baseline difficulty

P1 · ~2 days, needs token-level CE beside HC
Question
corr(gap, IG) = 0.96, open since v4. Does HC predict IG beyond token difficulty?
Design
Within deciles of CEbig, compute r(HC, IG); and the partial r(HC, IG | CEbig) at token level. Full token set, Qwen's tier-A cells first.
Statistic
Stratified r and its stability across deciles; partial against raw.
Decision rule
If the partial keeps 60% or more and the strata agree, the ‘where scale helps’ phrasing becomes defensible. Below 30%, the IG framing reduces to the difficulty gap.
